notes.meaning: A father calls on his child to welcome godly instruction and keep it close. God's truth cannot help us if we leave it on the outside and never take it to heart. We must store up His commands inside ourselves like a precious family treasure.

Gaining wisdom requires both our ears and our hearts. Listening with the ear means paying close attention when truth is spoken. Applying the heart means truly wanting to understand and obey it, rather than just hearing the words casually.

Finding true insight also requires earnest prayer. We cannot rely only on our own thinking to figure out life; we must ask God to give us understanding. Like a hungry child crying out for food, we need to pray eagerly for His help.

Wisdom is compared to buried treasure that takes hard work to find. Just as miners dig deep into the earth and sift through dirt to find silver, we must work hard to learn God's truth. God does not reveal His greatest wisdom to people who treat it as a casual hobby.

When someone seeks wisdom with all their strength, God rewards them with a real knowledge of Himself. Understanding the fear of the Lord means learning how to revere and honor Him with deep respect. This leads to a close, personal relationship with God that shapes daily life.

The Lord Himself is the only true source of wisdom, and He gladly gives it to those who ask. Knowledge and good judgment come directly from His mouth through His revealed word. Because He speaks to us through the Scriptures, we can completely rely on what He teaches.

God stores up practical, solid wisdom for people who are honest and upright. He also acts like a shield, protecting those who walk with integrity and keep clean consciences. Even when hard times come, God keeps them safe from real and lasting harm.

God watches over the path of right living and guards those who belong to Him. His saints are His devoted people whom He loves and protects. By keeping them safe on the right track, He helps them stay faithful to the very end.

Along with knowing God, wisdom teaches us how to treat other people with fairness. It gives clear moral guidance so we can tell right from wrong in every situation. God writes these principles on our hearts to lead us along every good road in life.

True wisdom does far more than fill our heads with ideas; it enters the heart and changes what we desire. When that happens, doing what is right stops feeling like a burdensome chore. God's truth becomes a sweet delight and brings deep joy to the soul.

Discretion means the ability to think ahead and make sound choices. When God's truth lives inside us, this good judgment acts like a personal guard. It keeps us from making foolish decisions and protects us from falling into harm.

Wisdom protects us from the danger of bad company. It rescues us from people who twist the truth and speak against what is good. Avoiding deceptive and rebellious voices keeps us from being dragged into spiritual ruin.

The teacher warns about people who once knew what was right but walked away from it. They abandoned the honest paths of God's word to follow their own dark desires in secret. Walking in spiritual darkness blinds people to danger and leads them far away from God.

These corrupt people have sunk so deep into sin that they actually enjoy doing wrong. They celebrate evil deeds and take pleasure in seeing others pulled into the same trap. Their twisted delight shows how hardened their hearts have become.

People who reject wisdom take crooked and deceitful roads in life. They use excuses and sneaky tricks to dodge their guilty consciences and avoid being corrected. Because they refuse to walk in the light of truth, they cannot be trusted.

Wisdom also protects a person from sexual sin and unfaithfulness. The forbidden or strange woman describes someone who lives outside God's moral boundaries and uses flattering words to trap others. God's truth helps a person see through those sweet lies before getting trapped.

This unfaithful woman breaks two sacred promises. She abandons the husband she married in her youth, and she ignores the marriage covenant she made before God. Marriage is a solemn promise witnessed by the Lord, and breaking it is a sin against Him.

Visiting the house of an unfaithful person is a quick road to ruin. Giving in to secret sexual sin destroys a person's life and leads straight toward God's judgment and death. Following her footsteps leads downward to the realm of the dead.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars note that the word for departed spirits (Rephaim) refers to the shadowy, weakened inhabitants of the underworld, rather than physical giants as some older translations suggested.

notes.meaning: Those who get trapped in deep sexual sin rarely find their way back. The deceitful pleasure of that sin hardens the heart and blinds the mind to truth. Without a special work of God's grace, very few ever return to the path of real life.

Wisdom has a positive goal: helping us follow the good examples of faithful people who went before us. Avoiding evil clears the way for us to walk alongside those who love God. Wisdom gives us the staying power to keep walking in their righteous steps.

Under God's covenant with Israel, faithful and blameless people were promised a peaceful home in the promised land. Walking with integrity brings stability, peace of mind, and the Lord's favor. This earthly blessing also points toward the eternal home God prepares for His people.

In contrast, those who rebel against God and act faithlessly will lose everything. God will pull them out of the land like weeds pulled up by their roots. Sin may seem harmless or exciting for a time, but it brings total and lasting destruction in the end.
